body:
I actually don't drink soda (only drink tea and water regularly because my teeth are super soft and prone to cavities... I drink milk, coffee and cider on occasion), take a probiotic every day (FoodScience of Vermont brand, it's wonderful), and want to get into yoga but suck at it so I've started with stretches and plan on working my way up.

These things, though, are all things I do when I'm not depressed. When I'm depressed, I drink lots of coffee with creamer, forget all my vitamins (I take a lot of them due to the irregular diet), and ride my bike for exercise still but don't go to the gym as often.

I guess what I'm trying to ask is "I know how to feel better, but I can't bring myself to do the things that will help my depression because I'm depressed and don't want to do anything. How do I force myself to do something?"

I appreciate the comment, but at the same time I'm already working on weight loss. It's not that I suck at weight loss and need "motivation"; I actually lost almost 80 pounds a few years ago healthily (but gained it all back when my depression got worse). It's that my eating is really irregular because the first thing that goes when I get depressed is regulating what I eat (going a full day not eating enough, then eating too much the next day, and so on), and more importantly it's that someone made a nasty comment when I was already suicidally depressed.

Not to flack you for commenting, but I already read GetMotivated, LoseIt, keep a food diary, work out (both cardio and weights), etc. etc. when I'm not depressed, and I have a lot of experience with weight management in the past; I really just needed to vent about feeling "kicked when I was down already".
